title: Combining Efflux Pump Inhibition with Low-Dose Beta-Lactams to Slow Resistance Emergence in E. coli
hypothesis: Pairing an efflux pump inhibitor with sub-inhibitory beta-lactam doses reduces the rate at which resistant Escherichia coli strains emerge in a simulated serial-passage experiment, compared with beta-lactam treatment alone.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance threatens the effectiveness of standard antibiotic therapy. We test whether combining an efflux pump inhibitor with low-dose beta-lactam treatment slows the emergence of resistance in a simulated population of Escherichia coli. Using a stochastic serial-passage model calibrated on published mutation and efflux parameters, we compare 30 replicate populations under combination therapy against 30 under beta-lactam monotherapy. Combination therapy delayed the median time to resistance fixation from 14 to 22 passages, a statistically significant difference (Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.004) with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.82). The 95% confidence interval for the delay was 4.1 to 11.6 passages. These results suggest that efflux inhibition is a promising adjuvant strategy, and they motivate wet-lab validation with clinical isolates.

retrieved_papers.title: Global trends in beta-lactam resistance in Escherichia coli
retrieved_papers.abstract: We review surveillance data on beta-lactam resistance in Escherichia coli and show a steady rise in resistant isolates, driven by mutation and horizontal gene transfer under antibiotic pressure.

retrieved_papers.title: Efflux pumps and low-level antibiotic tolerance
retrieved_papers.abstract: Efflux pumps expel antibiotics from bacterial cells. We show that efflux activity lets Escherichia coli survive sub-inhibitory beta-lactam doses and acts as a stepping stone towards resistance.

retrieved_papers.title: Stochastic models of combination antibiotic therapy
retrieved_papers.abstract: We model bacterial populations under combination therapy and show that drug pairs can delay the emergence of resistance in serial-passage simulations.

retrieved_papers.title: Mutation supply and the speed of resistance evolution
retrieved_papers.abstract: Higher mutation supply accelerates resistance fixation. We estimate mutation rates for resistance in Escherichia coli populations exposed to antibiotics.

retrieved_papers.title: Efflux pump inhibitors as antibiotic adjuvants
retrieved_papers.abstract: Efflux pump inhibitors restore antibiotic susceptibility in resistant bacteria and are being explored as adjuvants to beta-lactam therapy.
